stem: A historian studying the colonial economies of the Americas would see the steep population decline of the 1500s as most directly contributing to which of the following?

explanation: Native American populations had never encountered smallpox, measles, or influenza, so they had no acquired immunity. stem: Which of the following best explains why the League of Nations failed to stop Italy's invasion of Ethiopia?

explanation: Mussolini's invasion was one of three fascist aggressions of the 1930s: Japan seized Manchuria in 1931, Italy invaded Ethiopia in 1935, and Germany remilitarized the Rhineland in 1936. Together they exposed the collapse of the post-World War I peace settlement.

stem: Guaman Poma, an indigenous Andean, writes in Spanish to the Spanish king while holding colonial offices. What does this best demonstrate about Spanish colonial society?
stimulus: Adapted from Felipe Guaman Poma de Ayala, The First New Chronicle and Good Government, c. 1615: "I praise the ability of my son Don Felipe Guaman Poma de Ayala - capac, head governor and lord of the Indians, administrator of their common property, and deputy corregidor of the province of Lucanas. For twenty years he has been writing the history of our ancestors and of the kings from before the Inca and after, gathered from eyewitness testimony in the four quarters of these kingdoms. May Your Majesty grant him favor so his work may be published, celebrating the memory of the great lords who were our ancestors. May Your Majesty live and prosper, and add many more kingdoms to your dominions." Context: Guaman Poma was an indigenous Andean nobleman writing to the king of Spain; his 1,200-page chronicle wove together Quechua and Spanish perspectives and included hundreds of his own drawings.

explanation: 'Capac' is a Quechua title of Andean lordship; 'corregidor' is a Spanish colonial magistracy. One man holding both shows the two systems of authority fused in colonial Peru — neither purely Andean nor purely Spanish, but a hybrid.

option_explanations.B: Wrong. The direction of conquest was Spanish over Andean, not the reverse.
option_explanations.C: Wrong. Noble titles — both Andean and Spanish — remained central to colonial status.
option_explanations.D: Correct. The mixed titles embody the cultural blending of the colonial Andes.

stem: Busbecq describes European forces as divided and demoralized while the Ottomans are disciplined and united. Which of the following sixteenth-century developments best explains the European disarray he observed?
stimulus: Adapted from Ogier Ghiselin de Busbecq, Austrian ambassador to the court of Suleiman the Magnificent, The Turkish Letters, c. 1581: "On their side: a mighty and wealthy empire, great armies, experience in war, veteran soldiers, a long series of victories, patience in toil, concord, order, discipline, frugality, and vigilance. On our side: public want, private luxury, strength weakened, minds discouraged, soldiers disobedient, commanders greedy, contempt of discipline, licentiousness, rashness, drunkenness. They are accustomed to conquer; we, to be conquered. Only the Persian stands between us and ruin - the Turk's war with Persia gives us respite, not deliverance."

explanation: The janissaries were a standing professional infantry — recruited through the devshirme, trained from youth, paid in cash, and armed with firearms. They embodied the discipline, order, and permanence that Busbecq admired and found lacking in European feudal levies.

option_explanations.A: Wrong. The Ottomans relied on professional troops, not untrained peasant levies.
option_explanations.B: Wrong. The Ottomans maintained a powerful navy in the Mediterranean.
option_explanations.C: Wrong. The Ottomans were pioneers in the large-scale use of gunpowder artillery and muskets.
option_explanations.D: Correct. The janissary corps was the disciplined standing army Busbecq describes.

options: (A) The reliance on untrained peasant levies for all warfare.

option_explanations.A: Wrong. China had abundant metal for coinage; metal shortage was not the reason.
option_explanations.B: Wrong. No European demand drove Chinese monetary policy in the 1300s.
option_explanations.C: Correct. A commercialized economy with heavy transaction volume made paper currency practical and desirable.

stem: China used paper currency centuries before any other civilization. Which of the following developments best explains why paper money emerged in China first?
stimulus: Image: a Ming dynasty paper banknote (baochao) issued under the Hongwu Emperor, c. 1375. The large rectangular note is printed with Chinese characters stating its denomination - one string (1,000 copper cash) - and bordered with a pattern of interlocking coins. An official red seal is stamped at the center. A printed warning reads: "Counterfeiters shall be decapitated; informers shall receive a reward of 250 taels of silver." Source: British Museum.

explanation: A paper note is worthless in itself — its value rests entirely on public confidence that it will be accepted. Counterfeiting destroys that confidence, so the state treated it as an attack on the currency system itself, punishable by death.

option_explanations.A: Wrong. The Ming did not execute people for all minor offenses; the severity was specific to currency crimes.
